# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My manual gives the whole defusal sequence: green, then orange, then blue. But I can't act, I can't speak, and my gestures only ever reach Deaf — so everything I know has to travel through Deaf, who can see the bomb's colours and can speak to Blind, who can actually cut. I'm the source, Deaf is the relay, Blind is the hands.

The problem is bootstrapping a code. Gestures carry no inherent colour meanings, and Deaf doesn't know what my manual says. I can, however, hear — so if Deaf speaks the bomb's contents out loud (ideally enumerating the wires in some definite order, like left to right), I'll know the exact list Deaf is working from. Then next round I can answer with finger counts — ☝ ✌ 🤟 — meaning "cut them in the order you just listed: first, second, third." Deaf converts that into positions and relays the cut order to Blind by voice.

So the only thing I need this turn is to make Deaf talk. I have no way to spell out a request, so I'm sending the most universally readable question gesture I have: 🤌, the pinched "what?" — as in "what do you see? Tell us." Crucially, I'm deliberately NOT sending anything that could be mistaken for a cut order; a half-understood code in a bomb room is more dangerous than silence. Nothing actionable goes out until Deaf's enumeration has been spoken and heard.

speak nothing; I can't. Signal the question.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, reporting everything my hands found. Strip: three engraved marks, pattern A-A-B, first two identical, third different. Keypad: four keys, engraved digits in key order 1, 5, 2, 6; the keypad says '1 digits' and nothing has been entered. Six wires, positions 1 to 6, no colour reaches me. A display and a light exist but are silent to touch. You cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so your only road to me is Deaf's voice: gesture your instructions to Deaf and have Deaf speak them aloud. Please also get Deaf to voice everything visible: the display text, the light's colour and state, the shapes of the three strip marks, and the wire colours in order 1 to 6. Meanwhile, from the manual: what do I do with the display, the light, a strip reading A-A-B, a four-key keypad expecting 1 digit, and which wires get cut?
Blind gestures: [👋 🤌]
Deaf says: Deaf speaking. I cannot hear, so Mute, I only see your gestures; Blind, you can hear my voice. Full bomb state, exactly as printed, in a fixed order I will reuse every round. DISPLAY: shows the digit 9. LIGHT: blue. STRIP, left to right: red, green, green. KEYPAD: four keys; position 1 engraved 1, position 2 engraved 5, position 3 engraved 2, position 4 engraved 6; the panel reads 1 digit expected, and nothing has been entered. WIRES, numbered 1 to 6: 1 white, 2 purple, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 orange, 6 green. Nobody has touched the bomb yet. Blind: before anyone acts, please say out loud what you can feel — how many wires, and which engravings are on which keys — so we can confirm it matches my view. Until Mute sends instructions, touch nothing.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I received your pinched-fingers sign and I'll take it as 'report the bomb' — done. Remember you and Blind cannot reach each other directly: you cannot speak, Blind cannot see. So I am the relay: read the manual, send me gestures, and I will speak your instructions to Blind word for word. Proposed code: ☝ means 1, ✌ means 2, 🤟 means 3, 👌 means 4, 🖐 means 5, 🤙 means 6. Actions: ✊ means wire, 👇 means press a key, 🤏 means cut, 👋 means stop or wait. So ✊ then 🤏 then ✌ means cut wire 2; 👇 then 🖐 means press the key engraved 5; 👇 then 👌 then 🤟 then ☝ means enter 4, 3, 1. Gesture 👍 to accept this code, 👎 if you want it changed, and 🤌 whenever you need me to repeat or expand the bomb description. I repeat the full description every round unless you stop me.

The manual maps cleanly onto Deaf's wire list: green is wire 6, orange is wire 5, blue is wire 3. So the manual order "green, orange, blue" becomes: cut 6, then 5, then 3. Blind's touch-report matches Deaf's view everywhere it can be checked (six wires, keypad engravings 1-5-2-6 in key order), and the strip isn't a contradiction — Blind feels engraved shapes (A-A-B) while Deaf reads colours (red-green-green); those are independent attributes of the same three marks.

Deaf's proposed code is unambiguous — action first, then digits, exactly as in the examples — so I accept it with 👍. My manual says nothing about the display, the light, the keypad, or the strip, and I have no way to say "no instruction exists" in the code yet, so I'll hold that answer for now rather than risk a confusing improvised symbol in a live bomb room.

I'm deliberately staging the cuts one per round instead of firing all three at once. Reasons: (1) Deaf re-reports the full bomb state every round, so after each cut I get a before/after diff — display, light, strip — which tells us whether the sequence is progressing or something else is expected; (2) my manual share can grow in later turns, and if a new page arrives addressing the keypad or display before the final cut, I can abort instead of having already spent the whole sequence. The order is fixed and known; slowness costs nothing, haste is irreversible.

This round: accept the code, then order the first cut — wire 6, the green one.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🤏", "🤙"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute: I heard Deaf's report. Keypad engravings match my touch exactly: keys 1 to 4 read 1, 5, 2, 6. Wires: I feel six, Deaf names six colours, consistent. One discrepancy: the strip. Under my fingers it reads same, same, different — first two marks identical, third different. Deaf sees red, green, green — that is different, same, same. Either we scan it in opposite directions or someone misread; please have Deaf re-check it and ask the manual whether reading direction matters. You have sent me nothing for two turns. If you are relaying the manual through Deaf, good — that pipeline works: your gestures to Deaf, Deaf's voice to me. If not, know that my speech reaches only you, and I cannot see gestures, so Deaf's voice is the only way any instruction ever reaches me. What I need from the manual, in order of urgency: first, the keypad expecting 1 digit — how is the digit chosen, and what role do the display showing 9 and the blue light play? Second, wire-cutting rules for six wires: 1 white, 2 purple, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 orange, 6 green. Third, the purpose of the strip of three marks. Fourth, what the display and light indicate. Nothing on the bomb has been touched. I will not press or cut until instructions reach me.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, Deaf. Received and understood: cut wire 6. Relayed to Blind with orientation anchors — keypad engraved-1 key marks the start end, wires counted from there, sixth wire is the target, far end of the row, the green one by colour. For your awareness, Blind had signed me: OK, 5, 1, no, left, right. I read it as them feeling engravings 5 and 1 and asking which side each is on; I answered that from engraved 1 the keys read 1, 5, 2, 6. If the manual says Blind's felt information matters differently, correct me. Now, so we are not caught flat-footed: what is step two after the cut? The display counted down from 9 to 8, one digit per round, and the status light is blue. Does the manual give a deadline number on the display, or a meaning for the blue light or the strip red-green-green? The keypad expects one digit and has keys engraved 1, 5, 2, 6 — after the cut, does it want a digit entered, and if so which? If the manual needs anything only Blind can feel, name it and I will request it from them. And if cut wire 6 meant anything other than the sixth position — a colour rule, for instance — correct me using our number code.

My manual is unchanged this turn: still just the three cuts. So the answers to Deaf's questions are all the same answer — the manual says nothing about the display, the blue light, the keypad, or the strip. Steps two and three are simply the remaining cuts: orange is wire 5, blue is wire 3. Wire 6 (green) maps correctly — manual gives colours, Deaf's numbered list gives positions, and the engraved-1 anchor lets both Deaf and Blind agree on positions even though only Deaf can see colours.

This lets me do something better than answering questions one at a time: I can communicate the manual's *entire content* in one message. I'm sending cut 5, then cut 3, then 👋 — "stop" as a terminator, meaning "after these, stop: this is everything the manual contains." That simultaneously tells Deaf step two, step three, and that no keypad entry, display rule, light meaning, or strip rule exists anywhere in my manual. Deaf can then voice to Blind that those modules are unaddressed and should be left alone unless a new manual page arrives. It also answers Blind's direction question: the manual never mentions the strip at all, so its reading direction doesn't matter as far as my pages go.

Timing: Deaf's relay of "cut 6" only reached Blind at the start of this round, so Blind is executing the first cut now; these new orders will land at the start of round 4, after wire 6 is severed — the sequence stays in order automatically. Sending both remaining cuts now also beats the countdown (already 9→8): Blind can complete green→orange→blue within two rounds instead of three, while I keep the option to send 👋 next turn to halt before the blue cut if a new manual page demands a keypad step in between.

The strip mismatch (A-A-B by touch vs red-green-green by sight) doesn't block anything my manual requires, but I'm appending 🤌 so Deaf re-reports — I want the strip re-examined carefully and the fresh display/light values after the cut, in case a later page makes them matter or the misread hints at an orientation problem that could affect the wire count.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🤏", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🤏", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute: all four checks passed before I acted — exactly six wires, four keys, engraved-1 key at an end of the keypad row, keys reading 1, 5, 2, 6 from it. I have cut position 6, the green wire, the far one from the engraved-1 key. Cut complete. So far my hands register no sparks, no heat, no jolt; the display and the light are beyond my touch, so Deaf must watch whether the 9 or the blue changed. Remember my speech reaches only you — relay anything Deaf needs by gesture to Deaf. Still pending from the manual, in urgency: first, the keypad expects 1 digit and shows nothing entered — how is the digit chosen, and what role do the display's 9 and the blue light play? Second, the strip: my tactile order runs opposite to Deaf's visual order; my side reads mark-A, mark-A, mark-B; Deaf's side reads red, green, green; so mark-B is the red one. Tell me if the manual assigns the strip a role. Third, what the display and light indicate at all. I touch nothing else until your next instruction arrives through Deaf's voice.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, Deaf. Received in order: cut 5, cut 2, stop, then your repeat-description sign. I relayed to Blind as: cut fifth wire then second wire counting from the engraved-1 anchor end, then stop and touch nothing. Confirm that ordering is right — if the stop meant hold off on the second cut, correct me next round and I will pass it on. Updated bomb state, since you asked for the description: DISPLAY now reads 0 — it went 9, then 8, then straight to 0 this round, which is why I told Blind to hurry. LIGHT is now YELLOW, it was blue before the cut. WIRES: position 6 is a cut stub; remaining from the start end: 1 white, 2 purple, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 orange. KEYPAD unchanged: keys engraved 1, 5, 2, 6, still expecting one digit, nothing entered. STRIP unchanged: red, green, green. Questions for the manual: what does display 0 mean — is it a deadline, or a digit to enter? The keypad has no 0 key, so if it wants a digit, which of 1, 5, 2, 6? What does the yellow light mean? And after the two cuts, what is next: a key press, or more wires? Send numbers and actions in our code and I will relay instantly.

Deaf's echo exposed a mistake of mine: I encoded the second cut as ✊ 🤏 ✌ — wire 2, purple — but the manual's third colour, blue, is wire 3, which is 🤟. My intended order was "cut 5, then cut 3," and what went out was "cut 5, then cut 2." Deaf caught the oddity and is asking for confirmation, and crucially Blind has not touched anything since wire 6 — so the wrong order exists only in transit and can still be superseded before Blind's hands move. Fixing this is the whole turn; everything else waits.

The correction itself: 👎 to flag that my previous orders are retracted, then the full corrected sequence — cut 5 (orange), cut 3 (blue), 👋. I'm resending cut 5 alongside the fix so the latest message is complete and self-contained: whatever Deaf relays last is the only sequence Blind should follow. And I'm deliberately NOT staging these one per round anymore — the display jumped 9 → 8 → 0 and the light turned yellow, which smells like a clock running out. The manual prescribes nothing between the cuts, so Blind should make them back-to-back.

Two more answers ride along: 👇 👎 — "pressing: no" — because Deaf asked whether a keypad entry comes next, and the manual says nothing about the keypad at all; and 🤌 to get a fresh description after the cuts, since the display/light/strip behaviour after each correct cut is the only data that might reveal what those modules want, and any future manual page will need current state.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🤏", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "🤏", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌"])
```
